body:
_Migrated from issue #879, filed 2026-07-13._

**Type:** internal audit finding (surfaced while root-causing #615). Affects every non-English locale, not just French.

## What

The SPA i18n catalog (`GET /api/v1/i18n/<locale>.json`) is derived from the compiled `.mo`, and `msgfmt` excludes `#, fuzzy` entries by default. Many SPA msgids were auto-translated by fuzzy-matching against a longer, similar existing msgid — which both marks them `#, fuzzy` (so they're dropped from the `.mo`) and often produces the *wrong* meaning. Result: the SPA `t()` falls back to the English source string, so the affected strings render in English for every locale.

`grep -c '^#, fuzzy' cps/translations/fr/LC_MESSAGES/messages.po` = **485** (main). Comparable counts in other locales.

Examples (French), all `#, fuzzy` → excluded → English on screen:
- `Your Library` → "Convertir la bibliothèque" (= "Convert the library")
- `Library` → "Dans la librairie" (= "In the bookstore")
- `Advanced` → "Recherche avancée" (= "Advanced search")
- `Search title, author…` → "Rechercher par titre/auteur" (**correct French** — proving the fuzzy flag alone, not bad French, is enough to drop a good translation)

## Impact

Every non-English user sees a pool of new-UI strings in English (or would see wrong translations if the fuzzy value were compiled). High reach — hits all localized installs.

## Fix direction

Two options (not mutually exclusive): (a) review + de-fuzzy the SPA-anchored msgids per locale behind a quality gate, and/or (b) change the auto-translation job so it does not fuzzy-match SPA bare labels against unrelated longer msgids in the first place. A `.po`-lint test could pin that SPA-anchored msgids are never left `#, fuzzy`.

The user-facing French subset is being fixed directly under #615 (with the reporter's exact list). This issue tracks the systemic pass so it isn't lost. See `notes/615-french-spa-i18n-DESIGN.md` for the full mechanism breakdown.

Related: #615
title: SPA i18n: fuzzy-flagged translations silently fall back to English across all locales
